 Advertisement Early voting begins Tuesday for runoff elections in Arkansas
 Early voting begins Nov. 24 for local runoff races in Elm Springs, Springdale, Fayetteville and Washington County's Justice of the Peace District 15. Eligibility depends on where voters live.

 Early voting begins Nov. 24 for local runoff races in Elm Springs, Springdale, Fayetteville and Washington County's Justice of the Peace District 15. Eligibility depends on where voters live.
 Updated: 7:31 AM CST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Tia Greene Multimedia Journalist WASHINGTON COUNTY, Ark. — Early voting for local runoff elections in Washington County begins Nov. 24, but not every voter will be eligible to participate.
 The runoff elections include the Elm Springs mayoral race, a Springdale City Council race, Fayetteville's Ward 4 race and Washington County Justice of the Peace District 15.
 Advertisement Because the elections are limited to specific areas, voters must be registered and live within the jurisdiction holding the runoff to be eligible to vote.
 For the Elm Springs mayoral race and Springdale City Council race, voters must live within the city limits. Those voting in the Fayetteville Ward 4 race must live in Ward 4, while voters participating in the Justice of the Peace District 15 race must live within that district.
 Washington County Elections Director Jennifer Price said the runoff elections are just as important as the general election.
 "That's where it does matter for your vote. You are one of a small number of individuals who come to the polls to vote, so your vote is helping to determine who that next representative will be," Price said.
 Voters can use VoterView to verify if you live in the areas required to vote, see sample ballots and find your Election Day polling location. 
 Early voting will only take place Nov. 24, 25, 27 and 30 from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at the Washington County Courthouse on College Avenue.
 Voters must bring an approved photo ID, such as a driver’s license or military ID.
 Election Day is Dec. 1, with polls open from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.
